name: Canny Edge Density Analysis
description: Measures edge density and spatial high-frequency structural variations using a modified Canny detection algorithm. AI generative models often produce unusually smooth contours or overly sharp synthetic edges that disrupt the natural statistical density of edges found in organic photographs.
algorithm: Double-Threshold Edge Topography and Density Profiling
mechanism: The algorithm applies non-maximum suppression and hysteresis thresholding to extract precise edge maps, calculating the local and global density of these boundaries. Natural photographs exhibit complex, fractal-like edge distributions dictated by organic lighting and physical textures. Conversely, AI-synthesized images—constrained by latent space decoding and convolutional upband-smoothing—often display homogenized edge densities, leaving 'hyper-sharp' focal points surrounded by artificially barren, smoothed areas devoid of true micro-texture.
parameters: Detector: Canny Gradient Kernel, Thresholds: Adaptive Hysteresis (T_low, T_high), Metric: Spatial Edge Concentration
accuracy: Moderate (70-80%) - Effective at highlighting non-photorealistic synthetic smoothing, but highly sensitive to aggressive compression.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated digital art, identifying aggressive synthetic smoothing, and uncovering impossible, homogenized edge uniformities.

references.title: Canny, J. (1986). A Computational Approach to Edge Detection. IEEE TPAMI.
Farid, H. (2016). Photo Forensics. MIT Press.

strengths:
• Extremely fast, lightweight spatial domain computation requiring minimal resources.
• Visually highlights structural and textural homogenizations caused by generative decoding algorithms.
• Efficiently parses both color and grayscale inputs across vastly diverse, cluttered scenes.
• Inherently resilient against basic color adjustments and global brightness shifting manipulations.
limitations:
• Forensic accuracy plummets drastically after structural-altering JPEG mass compression.
• Legitimate, organic depth-of-field blur (bokeh) from high-end lenses creates very similar smooth/barren edge barren spots.
• Struggles significantly to distinguish between diffusion AI and the aggressive denoising algorithms embedded in modern smartphones.
• Prone to false positives in naturally smooth environments (e.g., clear cloudless skies, blank interior walls).
